question: During the first 3 seconds of a discharge, a piston moves at a rate equal to 1 times the square of the elapsed time plus 6 times the elapsed time. The total distance the piston covers from the 0th to the 3rd second, taken as a plain number, is used as the release speed in metres per second of a projectile of mass 6000 g on the adjacent launcher. The energy the projectile carries because of its motion is recorded. The launcher fires 5 projectiles per magazine and 7 magazines are emptied in the trial, and all the energies add. The barrel is 1.2 m long. What is the total energy for the trial, in kJ?

A warehouse holds 374 pallets and 48 cages, and both are moved in equal-sized loads of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That load size is multiplied by 9, and 29 is then added to the result, to give the release speed in metres per second of a test trolley on the loading rail. The trolley has a mass of 17 kg and runs on a level track. The energy the trolley carries because of its motion at that speed is recorded by the bench logger. What is that energy, in kJ?

Between the 1st and the 3rd second of a stroke, a pump plunger advances at a rate equal to 3 times the square of the elapsed time plus 1 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that interval, taken as a plain number, has 29 subtracted from it, and what is left is the release speed in metres per second of a test slug whose mass is 60 kg. The slug is released along a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. The rig fires 7 identical slugs in a batch, so the batch energy is 7 times that value. A calibration allowance of 23 J is then subtracted from the batch energy. What figure remains, in J?

A hoist controller adds its two calibration constants 9 and 18, multiplies the sum by 4, and then subtracts 28, treating the result as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A load of mass 66 kg is accelerated at that rate by the cable. The force the cable must apply to the load is worked out and expressed in kilonewtons. The gantry carrying the cable is already under 26 kN of tension from its own weight, and a tensioning jack then adds another 22 kN. What is the total force in the gantry, in kN?

Between the 1st and the 3rd second of a run, a shaper ram travels at a rate equal to 5 times the square of the elapsed time plus 2 times the elapsed time. The total travel over that interval, taken as a plain number, is used as the release speed in metres per second of a test block of mass 55 kg on the bench beside it. The energy the block carries because of its motion is measured and expressed in kilojoules. A trigger circuit adds 3 kJ to that figure and a damper then absorbs 9 kJ. The machine completes 10 identical runs in a shift and the energies add. The ram stroke is 0.4 m. What is the shift total, in kJ?

The last line of the log is 21 kJ more than 8 times the kilojoule reading described below. A launch controller adds its two dial settings 6 and 9, multiplies the sum by 3, and then subtracts 5 to fix the release speed in metres per second of a trolley whose mass is 13 kg. The trolley is released along a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. That energy, expressed in kilojoules, is the reading the line above is built from. The rail sits 0.75 m above the floor. What is the last line of the log, in kJ?

The figure the bench prints last is 22 kN less than the kilonewton reading described below. During the first second of a stroke, a hydraulic ram advances at a rate equal to 4 times the square of the elapsed time plus 8 times the elapsed time. The total advance from the 0th to the 1st second, taken as a plain number, is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a carriage of mass 137 kg. The force the drive must apply to the carriage is calculated, and because a second identical carriage shares the same yoke the yoke force is 2 times that force, which is then expressed in kilonewtons. The ram runs at 210 bar. What figure does the bench print last, in kN?

A control cabinet has 12 identical contactors and exactly 2 of them close in any one configuration; the number of different configurations available is used as the acceleration setting, in metres per second squared, for a shuttle of mass 98000 g. The force the drive must apply to the shuttle to accelerate it at that rate is calculated and a tare of 18 N from the load cell is added to it. The result is expressed in kilonewtons. Because 2 shuttles run on each rail, and 11 rails share one anchor wall, the wall load is that value multiplied by 2 and then by 11. The cabinet runs at 415 V. What is the load on the anchor wall, in kN?

A depot holds 12 tow bars and 144 shackles, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. Subtracting 7 from that batch size gives the release speed, in metres per second, of a test trolley whose mass is 21000 g. The trolley is released along a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. A trigger coil adds 15 J to that figure, and a lamp circuit then adds a further 24 J. The whole measurement is repeated on 2 identical trolleys and the two totals add. What is the combined total, in J?

The figure the commissioning sheet ends on is 5 times a value that is 30 kJ more than the kilojoule reading described below. During the first second of a cycle, a press ram advances at a rate equal to 5 times the square of the elapsed time plus 4 times the elapsed time. The total advance from the 0th to the 1st second, taken as a plain number, is the release speed in metres per second of a test slug whose mass is 28 kg. The energy the slug carries because of its motion is measured and expressed in kilojoules to give that reading. The ram bore is 90 mm. What figure does the commissioning sheet end on, in kJ?

Between the 2nd and the 3rd second of a stroke, a shuttle moves at a rate equal to 5 times the square of the elapsed time plus 2 times the elapsed time. The total distance it covers over that one-second interval, taken as a plain number, is the release speed in metres per second of a test mass of 27000 g on the rail beside it. The energy that mass carries because of its motion is recorded. The rig runs 4 identical masses in a batch and their energies add, after which a calibration offset of 28 J and then a further offset of 24 J are subtracted from the batch figure. The rail is 2.5 m long. What figure remains, in J?

A workshop holds 43 drill bits and 137 collets, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That batch size is the release speed, in metres per second, of a test trolley whose mass is 26000 g on a level bench. The energy the trolley carries because of its motion is recorded, and a calibration offset of 19 J is then subtracted from it. The bench runs 6 identical trolleys and the corrected energies add. That total is expressed in kilojoules, and because the same test is run on 5 benches the site figure is 5 times it. What is the site figure, in kJ?

During the first 2 seconds of a lift, a hoist drum pays out cable at a rate equal to 1 times the square of the elapsed time plus 3 times the elapsed time. The total length paid out from the 0th to the 2nd second, taken as a plain number, is doubled, and the result is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a skip whose mass is 75000 g. The force the cable must apply to the skip to accelerate it at that rate is calculated. A friction allowance of 18 N and then a windage allowance of 11 N are subtracted from that force. Because 12 identical skips hang from one headgear beam, the beam load is 12 times what is left. The drum turns at 45 rpm. What is the beam load, in N?

The number the log ends with is 8 times the kilojoule figure described below. A depot holds 313 rail clips and 24 keys, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That batch size is the release speed, in metres per second, of a test trolley of mass 23000 g on a level rail. The energy the trolley carries because of its motion is recorded, a trigger coil adds 27 J to it, and a lamp circuit adds a further 27 J. That combined figure, expressed in kilojoules, is what the number above is built from. What number does the log end with, in kJ?

The value the bench reports at the end is 7 times a figure that is 30 kJ less than a figure that is itself 23 kJ more than the kilojoule reading described below. A crate of 289 washers and a crate of 215 pins are both emptied into equal-sized trays of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either crate. That tray size is the release speed, in metres per second, of a test block whose mass is 18 kg on a level bench. The energy the block carries because of its motion is measured and expressed in kilojoules to give that reading. What value does the bench report, in kJ?

The quantity the rig finally reports is the energy of motion, in joules, of a carriage whose mass is 19 kg. Its release speed in metres per second is built up as follows. A depot holds 89 sleepers and 196 clips, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That batch size has 10 added to it, then 7 added to that, and then 9 taken away, and the result is the speed in metres per second at which the carriage is released along a level rail. What does the rig report, in J?

A patch panel has 8 identical sockets and any 2 of them may be linked; the number of different links that can be made is used as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a test mass of 8000 g on the bench beside it. The force needed to accelerate the test mass at that rate is calculated. A tare of 14 N from the load cell is added to it, and a preload of 7 N is added after that. The result is multiplied by 12 because 12 identical masses hang from one beam, and the whole beam is then repeated across 12 bays with the loads adding. The panel is rated at 48 V. What is the total load, in N?

The number the controller displays at the end is 25 kN less than the kilonewton figure described below. A press takes the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, adds 30 to it, then adds 2 more, and reads the result as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A ram of mass 148000 g is accelerated at that rate. The force the drive must apply to the ram to accelerate it that hard is calculated and expressed in kilonewtons to give that figure. What number does the controller display, in kN?

During the first second of a cycle, a shuttle on a bottling line moves at a rate equal to 1 times the square of the elapsed time plus 2 times the elapsed time. The total distance it covers from the 0th to the 1st second, taken as a plain number, has 10 added to it, and the result is the release speed in metres per second of a carrier whose mass is 31 kg. The energy the carrier carries because of its motion is recorded. The line runs 12 carriers per lane, 6 lanes per machine and 9 machines in the hall, and all the energies add. What is the total energy for the hall, in J?

A relay board has 9 identical contacts and any 2 of them may be bridged; the number of different pairs available is used as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a test mass of 32 kg on the bench beside it. The force needed to accelerate that mass at that rate is calculated. Because 11 identical masses hang from one beam, the beam load is 11 times that force, and a 1 N tare from the load cell is then added. The whole beam assembly is repeated across 10 bays and the loads add. The board runs at 24 V. What is the total load, in N?

A test rig sets its acceleration, in metres per second squared, from the sum of the squares of the whole numbers from 1 to 5. A carriage of mass 141000 g is accelerated at that rate along a level rail. The force the drive must apply to the carriage is calculated, and a tare of 18 N from the load cell is added to it. That total is expressed in kilonewtons, and a static frame preload of 2 kN is then added. What load does the frame carry, in kN?

The number the log records at the end is 11 times the newton figure described below. A hoist takes the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0, adds 10 to it, and reads the result as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A cage of mass 196000 g is lifted with that acceleration and the force the cable must apply to the cage is calculated. A friction allowance of 21 N is subtracted from that force and a preload of 19 N is then added, which gives the newton figure in question. The shaft is 60 m deep. What number does the log record, in N?

A launcher takes the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 14x + 48 = 0 and reads it as a release speed in metres per second. A dart of mass 28000 g is released at that speed along a level rail. The energy the dart carries because of its motion is recorded, and because 12 darts are fired from a magazine the magazine energy is 12 times that value. The magazine energy is expressed in kilojoules, and since 10 magazines are emptied in the trial the trial energy is 10 times that. A calibration allowance of 24 kJ is finally subtracted. What figure remains, in kJ?

The value the test bench prints at the end is 4 times a figure that is itself 10 times a value 19 kJ below the kilojoule reading described below. A trolley of mass 24 kg is released along a level rail, and its release speed in metres per second is the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0. The energy the trolley carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules to give that reading. The rail sits 1.1 m above the floor. What value does the test bench print, in kJ?

A launcher takes the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 15x + 56 = 0 and adds 17 to it, reading the result as a release speed in metres per second. A slug of mass 35 kg is released at that speed along a level rail. The energy the slug carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. The rig fires 5 identical slugs in a batch and the energies add. The rail is 8 m long. What is the batch energy, in kJ?
